newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BONDRA BREAKS SLUMP WITH FOUR GOALS AS CAPS BEAT AVALANCHE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BONDRA BREAKS SLUMP WITH FOUR GOALS AS CAPS BEAT AVALANCHE.

text.p: Peter Bondra broke out of a slump with a four-goal game and Joe Juneau added four assists as the Washington Capitals beat the Avalanche 6-3 Thursday, snapping Colorado's three-game winning streak.

Bondra had not scored a point in his last six games, but ended the drought early in the second period and scored the game's last three goals for his second hat trick of the season and ninth of his career. It was his third four-goal game.

"It feels good, especially after the slump I had," he said. "In a situation like that, you can't pull yourself down. Just stay positive and think about when you're scoring goals. And I knew the night would come.
"Just keep shooting the puck at the net, hopefully one or two would go in, and after, a bunch would go in.
"Tonight was the night."
Bill Ranford made 28 saves in his second start for Washington, improving his career mark against the Colorado-Quebec franchise to 16-6-1.

Peter Forsberg had a goal and an assist for the Avalanche, who lost for just the second time in their last seven road games. Mike Ricci and Valeri Kamensky also scored for the defending Stanley Cup champions while Adam Oates and Michal Pivonka had the other Washington talleys.

Patrick Roy got the night off after Wednesday's emotional return to Montreal and backup Craig Billington surrendered five goals on 15 shots over the final two periods. Billington shut out Washington in Denver in October.
"We weren't sharp," said Colorado coach Marc Crawford. "We don't give up three power-play goals very often."
At Tampa Bay, Nikolai Khabibulin made 30 saves for his second straight shutout and Mike Gartner scored twice as the Phoenix Coyotes coasted to a 5-0 rout of the Lightning.
Khabibulin, who stopped 14 shots in a 3-0 win over Florida Wednesday, turned aside seven in the first period, 14 in the second and 12 in the third en route to his seventh career shutout.
Since inheriting the number one job from the injured Darcy Wakaluk in early January, Khabibulin has made 26 straight starts, recording five shutouts.
Oleg Tverdovsky had a power-play goal and an assist and Craig Janney and Dallas Drake also scored for Phoenix, which tied St. Louis for fifth place in the Western Conference with 64 points.

On Long Island, Claude Lapointe and Marty McInnis each had a goal and an assist and Tommy Salo stopped 30 shots as the New York Islanders routed the Boston Bruins 5-2 in a matchup of the worst two teams in the Eastern Conference.
Salo, who has started 11 straight games, bounced back from a sub-par effort on Tuesday to stonewall the Bruins over the final two periods.
Derek King, Todd Bertuzzi and Dan Plante also tallied for the Islanders, who moved within five points of the final Eastern Conference playoff spot.
The Bruins lost All-Star defenceman Ray Bourque midway through the second period when he was hit in the right ankle by a puck. He was carried from the ice and did not return.

"They took an X-ray, which was negative," he said. "Not much you can do to keep the pain away. It's right under the ankle bone. A lot of swelling and pain right now, it's like a deep bruise. The trainer said to have treatments, sit tight, ice it and see how it responds in a couple of days."
At Los Angeles, six different players scored for the New York Rangers, who built a four-goal lead and cruised to a 6-2 victory over the Kings, breaking a seven-game road winless streak.
Mark Messier collected three assists and Wayne Gretzky, Niklas Sundstrom, Brian Leetch and Chris Ferraro each had a goal and an assist for the Rangers.
Glenn Healy, one of three former Kings in the New York lineup, turned aside 23 shots for his first win since January 22.
Ray Ferraro and Vitali Yachmenev tallied for Los Angeles, which has lost two in a row following a season-high five-game winning streak.
In San Jose, Ed Belfour stopped 29 shots for his first shutout with his new team and Viktor Kozlov and Tony Granato scored, leading the Sharks to a 2-0 victory over the slumping Ottawa Senators.

Belfour, making his sixth appearance with San Jose since he was acquired from Chicago on January 24, was at his best in the first period when he made 17 saves. He turned aside five shots in the second and seven in the third for his 31st career shutout.
